items.summary: Goolsbee argues central banks should not look through persistent supply shocks: if shocks are large and recurring, the only way to bring inflation down is to raise rates, though the response need not be as large as for demand overheating and will not be painless. AP and Axios report he told reporters the fight would be painful and that one hike likely would not be enough if inflation is demand-driven. coverage_notes: Sources used: the four banks' own speech and essay pages, the Chicago Fed speaking and media-appearance lists, and wire stories reached through those lists, earlier search results, and the Kitco (Reuters feed) and investingLive sitemaps filtered by speaker name. The web-search budget for this session ran out early, so later discovery relied on those lists and sitemaps rather than month-by-month searches. Thin coverage: June and July for all four speakers (Goolsbee 3 items, Barkin 2, Collins 0, Venable 0); the Kitco Reuters sitemap returned no speaker stories before Aug 7. Collins has no items before Aug 12; any June-July interviews were not found. Atlanta: Cheryl Venable (first vice president and COO) has been interim president since March 2026 after Raphael Bostic's term ended Feb 28; the Atlanta Fed speeches and media-interview feeds list nothing by her, so coverage is her two quarterly essays (Aug 11, Nov 17; the May 12 essay is before the window). The presidential search is still open. Goolsbee: many appearances are video or audio only or paywalled (CNBC Aug 28, Odd Lots, AP/NYT/WSJ at Jackson Hole, Fox Business, CNN, Bloomberg, Chosun) and sit in the unverified list with whatever paraphrase was visible. His Nov 2 Financial Markets Group appearance was as moderator and is not itemized. Barkin: Richmond Fed posts only prepared speeches (Aug 13, Sep 22, Nov 9); interviews come from wire recaps, some with short quoted fragments (flagged in score_note). Quote caveats: Two Goolsbee pages (Marketplace Jun 22, Chosun Oct 16) are script-rendered, so a plain HTTP fetch returns no article text; they were read in a browser and a substring check without JavaScript will not find the quotes. Kitco's copies of Reuters stories contain invisible zero-width characters inside sentences, so quotes sourced from Kitco were limited to spans without them (hence a few clipped quotes: Collins Aug 12, Sep 22). Yahoo Finance and WTTW/PBS transcripts are auto-generated captions, quoted as they appear on the page. Collins Oct 9 and Nov 13 (speech) quotes are from the official PDF texts. Reuters quotes Barkin's Aug 13 prepared text as 'Will the Fed need to raise rates or is inflation...' while the posted Richmond Fed text reads 'raise rates further'; the posted text is used. Times for Collins Oct 13 and Goolsbee Nov 12 come from the linked official PDF and the Chicago Fed event page, not the source_url page itself. Tagging: Goolsbee, Barkin, Collins and Venable repeatedly cite the AI data-center build-out as a demand-side inflation driver; this is tagged 'other', not 'ai_financing'. Only Goolsbee's Semafor interview (Oct 12) links policy to AI debt financing and hyperscaler debt issuance. Context checks: nothing contradicts the brief. Additional facts seen: the July 29 hold had three dissents in favor of a hike (Reuters); Reuters dates the next meeting December 8-9; Waller floated a 50bp December hike; Goolsbee dissented against the December 2025 cut; AP says Collins next votes in 2028.
